definitions.gloss: secret informing; tip-off; informing on someone
definitions.explanation: Secretly reporting someone's wrongdoing to the authorities or to someone in power. Carries a negative connotation of betrayal or disloyalty.

examples.japanese: {仲間|なかま}を{密告|みっこく}する。
{密告|みっこく}によって{犯人|はんにん}が{逮捕|たいほ}された。
examples.english: The criminal was arrested thanks to a tip-off.

examples.japanese: {戦時中|せんじちゅう}は{隣人|りんじん}による{密告|みっこく}が{恐|おそ}れられていた。
examples.english: During wartime, people feared being informed on by their neighbors.

notes:
{密告|みっこく} means secretly reporting someone's wrongdoing to authorities or those in power. It carries a strong negative connotation of betrayal and treachery.

COMPOUNDS:
- {密告|みっこく}{者|しゃ}: informer, snitch
- {密告|みっこく}{状|じょう}: letter of denunciation
- {匿名|とくめい}{密告|みっこく}: anonymous tip-off

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {密告|みっこく}: secret informing (negative — implies betrayal)
- {通報|つうほう}: reporting to authorities (neutral)
- {告発|こくはつ}: formal accusation, whistleblowing (can be positive)
- {告|つ}げ{口|ぐち}: tattling, telling on someone (childish)

ETYMOLOGY:
{密|みつ} (secret) + {告|こく} (inform, tell). The {密|みつ} emphasizes the secretive, underhanded nature of the act.

USAGE:
Often appears in historical and wartime contexts. In modern usage, also refers to anonymous tips to police or tax authorities.
